author: Thomas à Kempis
title: Of having confidence in God when evil words are cast at us

notes.text: (1) Luke ii. 35. (2) Proverbs xii. 21. (3) Psalm vii. 9. (4) 1 Corinthians iv. 4. (5) Psalm cxliii. 2.

verses.text: “My Son, stand fast and believe in Me.
verses.modernizedText: “My Son, stand firm and believe in Me.

verses.text: For what are words but words?
verses.modernizedText: For what are words but words?

verses.text: They fly through the air, but they bruise no stone.
verses.modernizedText: They fly through the air, but they bruise no stone.

verses.text: If thou are guilty, think how thou wouldst gladly amend thyself; if thou knowest nothing against thyself, consider that thou wilt gladly bear this for God’s sake.
verses.modernizedText: If you are guilty, think how gladly you would amend yourself; if you know nothing against yourself, consider that you will gladly bear this for God’s sake.

verses.text: It is little enough that thou sometimes hast to bear hard words, for thou art not yet able to bear hard blows.
verses.modernizedText: It is little enough that you sometimes have to bear harsh words, for you are not yet able to bear hard blows.

verses.text: And wherefore do such trivial matters go to thine heart, except that thou art yet carnal, and regardest men more than thou oughtest?
verses.modernizedText: And why do such trivial matters go to your heart, except that you are still carnal and regard people more than you ought?

verses.text: For because thou fearest to be despised, thou art unwilling to be reproved for thy faults, and seekest paltry shelters of excuses.
verses.modernizedText: Because you fear being despised, you are unwilling to be reproved for your faults and seek the paltry shelter of excuses.

verses.text: “But look better into thyself, and thou shalt know that the world is still alive in thee, and the vain love of pleasing men.
verses.modernizedText: “But look more closely into yourself, and you will know that the world is still alive in you, along with the vain love of pleasing others.

verses.text: For when thou fleest away from being abased and confounded for thy faults, it is plain that thou art neither truly humble nor truly dead to the world, and that the world is not crucified to thee.
verses.modernizedText: For when you flee from being humbled and confounded for your faults, it is plain that you are neither truly humble nor truly dead to the world, and that the world is not crucified to you.

verses.text: But hearken to My word, and thou shalt not care for ten thousand words of men.
verses.modernizedText: But listen to My word, and you will not care for ten thousand words of men.

verses.text: Behold, if all things could be said against thee which the utmost malice could invent, what should it hurt thee if thou wert altogether to let it go, and make no more account of it than of a mote?
verses.modernizedText: See, if everything that the utmost malice could invent were said against you, what harm would it do you if you simply let it go and regarded it as no more than a speck?

verses.text: Could it pluck out a single hair of thy head?
verses.modernizedText: Could it pluck out a single hair of your head?

verses.text: “But he that hath no heart within him, and hath not God before his eyes, is easily moved by a word of reproach; but he who trusteth in Me, and seeketh not to abide by his own judgment, shall be free from the fear of men.
verses.modernizedText: “But the one who has no heart within him and does not keep God before his eyes is easily moved by a word of reproach; but whoever trusts in Me and does not seek to rely on his own judgment will be free from fear of others.

verses.text: For I am the Judge and the Discerner of all secrets; I know how the thing hath been done; I know both the injurer and the bearer.
verses.modernizedText: For I am the Judge and Discerner of all secrets; I know how the thing was done; I know both the one who injures and the one who bears it.

verses.text: From Me went forth that word, by My permission this hath happened, that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed.(1) I shall judge the guilty and the innocent; but beforehand I have willed to try them both by a secret judgment.
verses.modernizedText: That word went forth from Me; by My permission this has happened, so that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed.(1) I shall judge the guilty and the innocent; but beforehand I have willed to test them both by a secret judgment.

verses.text: “The testimony of men often deceiveth.
verses.modernizedText: “The testimony of people often deceives.

verses.text: My judgment is true; it will stand, and it shall not be overturned.
verses.modernizedText: My judgment is true; it will stand and will not be overturned.

verses.text: It commonly lieth hid, and only to few in certain cases is it made known; yet it never erreth, nor can err, although it seem not right to the eyes of foolish men.
verses.modernizedText: It is usually hidden, and only in certain cases is it made known to a few; yet it never errs, nor can it err, although it does not seem right to the eyes of foolish people.

verses.text: To Me, therefore, must men have recourse in all judgment, and must not lean to their opinion.
verses.modernizedText: Therefore people must turn to Me in every judgment and must not rely on their own opinion.

verses.text: For there shall no evil happen to the just,(2) whatsoever may be sent to him by God.
verses.modernizedText: For no evil shall happen to the just,(2) whatever may be sent to him by God.

verses.text: Even though some unjust charge be brought against him, he will care little; nor, again, will he exult above measure, if through others he be clearly vindicated.
verses.modernizedText: Even if an unjust charge is brought against him, he will care little; nor will he rejoice excessively if he is clearly vindicated by others.

verses.text: For he considereth that I am He who try the hearts and reins,(3) who judge not outwardly and according to human appearance; for often in Mine eyes that is found blameworthy which in the judgment of men is held worthy of praise.”
verses.modernizedText: For he considers that I am He who tests the hearts and reins,(3) who does not judge outwardly or according to human appearance; for often what is held worthy of praise in human judgment is found blameworthy in My eyes.”

verses.text: O Lord God, O Judge, just, strong, and patient, who knowest the frailty and sinfulness of men, be Thou my strength and my whole confidence; for my own conscience sufficeth me not.
verses.modernizedText: O Lord God, O Judge, just, strong, and patient, who know the frailty and sinfulness of people, be my strength and my whole confidence; for my own conscience is not enough for me.

verses.text: Thou knowest what I know not; and therefore ought I under all rebuke to humble myself, and to bear it meekly.
verses.modernizedText: You know what I do not know; therefore I ought to humble myself under every rebuke and bear it meekly.

verses.text: Therefore mercifully forgive me as often as I have not done this, and grant me the next time the grace of greater endurance.
verses.modernizedText: Therefore mercifully forgive me whenever I have not done this, and grant me the grace of greater endurance next time.

verses.text: For better unto me is Thine abundant pity for the attainment of Thy pardon, than the righteousness which I believe myself to have for defence against my conscience, which lieth wait against me.
verses.modernizedText: For Your abundant pity, by which I may obtain Your pardon, is better for me than the righteousness I believe I possess as a defense against my conscience, which lies in wait against me.

verses.text: Although I know nothing against myself, yet I am not hereby justified,(4) because if Thy mercy were removed away, in Thy sight should no man living be justified.(5)
verses.modernizedText: Although I know nothing against myself, I am not thereby justified,(4) because if Your mercy were taken away, no living person would be justified in Your sight.(5)
